The Terrifying Experiment That Turned Students Into a Cult

What happens when an ordinary classroom begins to act like a cult? In just five days, a high school experiment transformed a group of students into a disciplined movement built around obedience, unity, and absolute loyalty.

In 1967, history teacher Ron Jones conducted an experiment at Cubberley High School in California to help students understand how ordinary people could become involved in authoritarian movements. What started as a classroom lesson about discipline and collective power quickly escalated into something deeply unsettling.

Known as The Third Wave Experiment, this controversial real-life experiment demonstrated how easily group identity, peer pressure, authority, and the desire to belong can influence human behavior.

In this documentary, we explore how the experiment began, why students embraced the movement, how its rules spread through the classroom, and what happened when the truth was finally revealed.

Was it simply a school lesson, or did it expose something disturbing about human psychology?

Watch until the end to discover the lessons behind one of the most fascinating and unsettling classroom experiments in modern history.
